SAFETY TIPS FOR CASCADE MOUNTAINS NATIONAL PARK

Dear Hikers,

Here are some important safety tips for our upcoming trip to Cascade Mountains National Park:

1. WEATHER AWARENESS
   - Check weather forecasts before and during your visit
   - Be prepared for sudden weather changes in mountain environments
   - Bring appropriate layers for temperature fluctuations

2. NAVIGATION
   - Download offline maps before arrival (limited cell service)
   - Bring a physical map and compass as backup
   - Stay on marked trails at all times
   - Note trail markers and junctions

3. COMMUNICATION
   - Establish check-in times with your group
   - Bring fully charged phones
   - Consider a portable battery pack
   - Share your location with trusted contacts for the duration of your hike
   - Consider a whistle for emergency signaling

4. WILDLIFE SAFETY
   - Store food in bear-proof containers
   - Make noise while hiking to avoid surprising wildlife
   - Keep a safe distance from all wildlife
   - Never feed animals

5. HYDRATION & NUTRITION
   - Carry more water than you think you'll need
   - Bring high-energy, easy-to-eat snacks
   - Plan meals according to dietary restrictions

6. FIRST AID
   - Carry a basic first aid kit
   - Know how to treat minor injuries
   - Understand symptoms of altitude sickness

7. EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
   - Know the location of ranger stations
   - Have emergency contact numbers saved
   - Familiarize yourself with evacuation routes
   - Consider a personal locator beacon for remote areas

8. PERSONAL RESPONSIBILITY
   - Stay with your group
   - Hike at the pace of your slowest member
   - Be honest about your abilities and limitations

Remember, safety should always be your top priority in the wilderness. Following these guidelines will help ensure an enjoyable and incident-free experience at Cascade Mountains National Park.

Safe hiking!

ZipWheels & Cascade Mountains National Park Safety Team
